confirmed.title: Editing an old Form response adds a second copy of a case the workbook import already brought in (and a re-import after a Form edit does the same)
confirmed.scenario: A. A resident submitted a Form response on 3 Oct, before the inbox went live, so it reached the logbook through the Admin workbook import (source 'import', createdAt = the sheet timestamp + 8 h). On 20 Oct they open the Form's 'Edit response' link to fix a typo. Response editing stays ON (owner, 14 Oct). The trigger fires (Code.gs: 'Edited responses fire it too') and sends the entry with submittedAt = response.getTimestamp(), which is now the edit time (form-inbox.js line 9: 'changes when the response is edited'). When the app picks it up there is no Form case with formCaseId, and isImportOf(imported, e) compares the import's createdAt (3 Oct) with the 20 Oct edit time. sameResponse fails because the gap is more than 14 h, so mergeFormEntries saves a new Form case. B. A response first brought in by the inbox is later edited in the Form, so its sheet row now carries the edit timestamp and the new text. The Form case keeps createdAt = the first submission (mergeFormEntries line 94). An admin or Firetop re-import (as on 14 Oct) then runs withoutFormCases (line 111): row.createdAt (edit time) never matches c.createdAt (first submission), and the edited row has a new content hash and importKey, so importCases writes it as a second case.
confirmed.consequence: One Form response becomes two cases in the logbook while the response sheet has one row, so Totals and Still needed count it twice and the app's counts no longer match the sheet. The resident sees the duplicate. Nothing removes it again: the Form copy has source 'form' and the import copy has its own id. Every one of the ~16,000 pre-inbox responses is exposed whenever its owner edits it.
confirmed.fix: Match on the response's first submission as well as its latest one. In Code.gs, send the response's first-submit time (`createTime` from the Forms API: the Forms advanced service, or UrlFetch with ScriptApp.getOAuthToken(); FormApp only gives the latest) as a new entry field (allowed in validFormEntry). isImportOf then accepts sameResponse against either time. For direction B, store the latest submittedAt in the Form case: importKey has room (<=200 chars), e.g. `form:<id>@<pickupMs>~<submittedAt>`. withoutFormCases then matches the row's timestamp against that as well as createdAt. A cheaper app-only stopgap: when the time check fails but an import case has the same date and the same initials, don't add the case; flag it to the resident instead.
verifier_fix:
The proposed direction works, with these gaps:
1. The import case's createdAt is the sheet timestamp at import time. That is the last submission before the import, not necessarily the Forms API createTime: if a response was edited before the import and again after it, neither time matches. So send createTime, but also tell the resident when an import case falls on the same day and has the same initials, rather than silently adding a second case.
2. sameDay is required in both isImportOf and withoutFormCases. An edit that fixes the date, a likely typo fix, still makes a duplicate even with createTime. When matching on createTime, relax sameDay to the exact sheet-zone offset (+8 h to the second) instead of any quarter-hour, which keeps false matches rare.
3. For direction B, a cheaper app-only fix is to stop keeping the first submission at form-inbox.js line 94 and set createdAt (or a recorded latest-submit time) to the newest submittedAt, so withoutFormCases matches the current sheet row. Also record the newest submittedAt on cases kept because the resident edited them in the app. Today those get no write, so the sheet row's new timestamp never matches.
4. Separate from the inbox: the workbook re-import already writes any row edited on the sheet side as a new import case, because of its new content hash and importKey; the drift-check skill notes an edit shows as "a missing and an extra row". Neither the claim's fix nor the ones above cover this, so it needs its own fix.
5. Add tests: an import followed by an edited inbox entry, and a Form case edited and then re-imported.

confirmed.title: A deleted Form case comes back when its response is sent again after the bin entry has gone (30-day purge, Delete forever, or a backfill that overlaps the import)
confirmed.scenario: 1) A resident logs a wrong case through the Form on 15 Oct; the app picks it up. 2) They delete it in the app (README: 'a wrong Form entry is deleted in the app (it won't come back)'). Then they press Delete forever in the bin, or 30 days pass and purgeExpired drops the bin entry. 3) The response is sent to the inbox again. Either the resident edits it in the Form to void it in the still-trusted sheet, or the owner runs logbookInboxBackfill to resend one failed response. The README gives the backfill as the remedy for a failed send, Code.gs:159 says 'Safe to run again', and its default SINCE is 1 Oct. 4) mergeFormEntries finds no case and no bin id (the only tombstone is the bin entry, and inBin is checked at line 86), so it writes the case back. Variant: a case from the 1–14 Oct workbook import that the resident deleted has an imp_ id in the bin, never the Form id, and it is no longer in `existing`, so isImportOf can't match it either. A backfill with the default SINCE brings it back as a Form case even while it is still in the bin. Separately, app.js:1086 turns a failed bin read into 'nothing deleted' (`cloud.listBin(user.email).catch(() => [])`).
confirmed.consequence: Cases the resident deliberately deleted reappear and count again in Totals. One backfill run can bring back every such deletion for every resident at once. This breaks the documented promise in README line 56 and Code.gs line 159.
confirmed.fix: Keep a durable tombstone for Form responses. When a source 'form' case is deleted, add its response id to a capped list on the logbook doc (e.g. `formGone`, allowed in validLogbook), or have purgeExpired/deleteForever keep a small tombstone for form cases. mergeFormEntries treats those ids as gone. For the import variant, also run isImportOf against the bin entries' `data`, not only live cases. In pickUpForm, stop the pick-up (don't fall back to []) when listBin fails. Correct the README and Code.gs wording until this is done.
verifier_fix:
The proposed direction is right. Some refinements:

1. **Keep a durable tombstone that also works for imports.** When a case with source 'form' or 'import' is deleted (in `moveToBin`, or at the latest in `purgeExpired` / `deleteForever`), keep a small record of it: `{id, date, dateText, createdAt}`. Store these as a capped list on the logbook doc, or in a new owner-only subcollection; either needs a rules change and `tools/test-rules.sh`. Then `mergeFormEntries` takes `tombstones` = the bin entries' data plus the durable list, and checks each response two ways:
   - an id match against `formCaseId`;
   - `isImportOf` against the tombstone data, not only against live cases.

   This covers both the purged form case and the deleted imported case. A list of form ids alone would miss the import variant once that entry's bin copy is purged.
2. **Read the bin reliably in `pickUpForm`.** Use a server read (`getDocsFromServer`), not `getDocs`, and stop the pick-up if the bin read fails. Do not fall back to [].
3. **Fix the backfill default and the wording now**, since that costs nothing and needs no rules change:
   - Set `SINCE` in `logbookInboxBackfill` to the inbox go-live date, after the last workbook import, to match README step 6.
   - Change the wording in Code.gs:158-159 and form-script/README.md:56 and 68-69 to "deleted cases still in the recycle bin" until step 1 ships.
4. **Add tests** for a purged or deleted-forever form case and for a deleted imported case.

confirmed.title: Form cases late in a pick-up are stamped as 'edited in the app', so later Form edits to them are silently dropped
confirmed.scenario: pickUpForm (app.js:1088) stamps every case once: importKey 'form:<id>@<now>' and updatedAt = now. commitFormPickup then loops over up to PICKUP_MAX = 50 entries. For each one it runs `cleanCase(it.case)`, which restamps updatedAt to Date.now() at that moment, then waits for the server (`await b.commit()`). Once the loop has spent more than SAVE_SLACK (10 s) on earlier commits, each later case's updatedAt is more than 10 s after its importKey time. That happens on a slow hospital connection with ~20+ entries, after one stalled commit (a lift, or patchy Wi-Fi), or when the resident switches away from the PWA right after opening it, which suspends the loop. From then on the case looks edited in the app (form-inbox.js:92). A week later the resident edits that response in the Form, e.g. adds a category. The pick-up puts it in `kept`, deletes the inbox entry and toasts '1 edited Form response left as you changed it here', although the resident never touched it in the app.
confirmed.consequence: The resident's correction never reaches the logbook while the response sheet has it, so a changed category makes app and sheet counts differ. The toast tells the resident something false, and the edit can't be recovered from the inbox because the entry has been deleted.
confirmed.fix: Take importKey's time from the stamp actually written. In commitFormPickup, after `const d = cleanCase(it.case)`, set `d.importKey = d.importKey.replace(/@\d+$/, '@' + d.updatedAt)`. Stamping at commit time is better than reusing the merge time because it keeps the write inside other devices' delta window.
